hardness_reason: All losses sit within ~0.4 of the ln(32)=3.47 random baseline after only 80 steps, and the references are internally inconsistent (tiny-lr RMSprop beats high-lr AdamW), so optimizer/lr effects are indistinguishable from run-to-run noise.

References only show SGD at a tiny lr (3e-4, barely training) and no SGD-with-momentum or RMSprop-at-0.01 point, so the optimizer/effective-lr axis that decides the winner is never probed, and the top candidates (F vs E vs C) differ by amounts likely near run-to-run noise.

Only one reference uses RMSprop (the best at 3.1882) and at a different lr, so the winner must be inferred by extrapolating optimizer strength rather than read off a varied axis; all SGD options with lr<=3e-4 are obviously near-untrained (~ln32=3.47), making D plausible but not strictly determined.

No reference uses Adam/AdamW, so the optimizer axis that most likely decides the winner never appears in the references, and the one RMSprop lr comparison available (3e-4 vs 1e-3) is confounded with depth/width changes.

The references only give one point per optimizer's lr curve, so the optimal learning rate for each optimizer family (esp. Adagrad 0.01 vs 0.001, RMSprop 1e-4 vs 3e-3) must be extrapolated, and several candidates plausibly land within noise of each other.

References only show one learning rate per optimizer, so the lr-vs-optimizer interaction must be extrapolated, and the several plausible low-lr adaptive options (A, B, F) are likely within noise of each other.

References only sample a coarse depth/width trend (wider+shallower is better) and never disambiguate the close cases (depth-4 width-256 vs depth-1 width-128), so the winner rests on extrapolation rather than logic.

References only show a coarse depth/width trend (shallower+wider better under SGD) and never isolate layer-norm, residual, or narrow-width effects, so distinguishing D from C/E requires guessing about underfitting.

References only show that wide (64) nets with layer norm hit the ~1e-4 floor while narrow/shallow ones fail, but four of the six options (B, C, E, F) all satisfy that condition, so the discriminating axes (width 256 vs 64, residual, LN placement, activation mix) are never varied in isolation and the gap between the top candidates is likely at noise level.

References establish a clear width/capacity trend (256-wide → 0.051, 128 → 0.058, 64 → 0.32, 32 → 0.65) so the widest option B is a reasonable inference, though the 0.051 vs 0.058 gap between the two large models is within likely seed noise and depth/layernorm/activation interactions are not isolated.

References only cover depth 3-5 and widths 16-128, showing narrow/no-residual is best, but three options use depth-1 wide nets whose behavior is never probed, so the winner's key axis (very shallow, very wide) is unrepresented.

References establish that LayerNorm presence and width>=32 matter (no-LN and width-16 runs are ~20-30x worse), but they don't disentangle depth vs. LN-fraction among the plausible candidates (B vs. D), whose expected gap is likely within run-to-run noise.

Width is the dominant driver in the references (w16→0.99, w64→0.66-0.73, w256→0.63-0.64), so A's width-32 net should sit above B's width-64 net, but A's depth-5 and B's untested residual connections add unquantified uncertainty that could easily flip a ~0.05-0.10 gap.

The references establish a clear width trend (256 → ~0.74-0.79, 64 → 0.87, 32 → 0.93), so the width-256 option is a straightforward extrapolation, though the residual-connection flag on B is unexplored in the references.

Depth is the dominant factor in the references (depth 5-6 → ~0.39-0.44 vs depth 2 → ~0.53-0.55) and B is even shallower with a small LR, though no depth-1 reference exists and the effect of A's high LR (0.003) is only sampled once.

The references cleanly isolate that layer norm rescues the tiny 1e-4 learning rate (ref 3 at 0.53 vs ref 2 at 0.76), so A's all-LayerNorm config is inferable, though depth-5 residual effects in B are only weakly constrained.

Depth appears to dominate (depth-2/width-128 = 0.399 vs deeper nets ≈ 0.09-0.13), so B (depth 2) likely loses to A (depth 3), but A's narrow width-32 puts it in a regime where reference losses vary wildly (0.13 to 0.65), leaving real ambiguity.

Width is a clean monotone signal in the references (128 → 0.058–0.075, 64 → 0.089–0.148), so B's narrower and shallower net is the safe pick, though depth-3 vs depth-5 at width 64 is untested and activation/layernorm patterns add unmodeled noise.
